Jaco Swart: Injustice served

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Assaulted, beaten and running for safety, Nicoleen Swart made headlines when she posted a video of her husband beating her up in his office. Now, the state has set him free.

Unique Selling Point:
In a country where GBV is rife, the state has freed up a women beater, seemingly turning a blind eye for his deeds. But the evidence is all there, aggression second to none, caught on camera in the act.

Summary:
When Nicoleen Swart released videos on social media of her husband beating her up, South Africans were furious. But more so, because she relied on the justice system to put him behind bars, and it failed her. Instead, the culprit, Jaco Swart, is now a free man. We investigate, why the state released Swart on bail and dismissed video footage of the assault. Private prosecutor, Gerrie Nel has taken over the case and his team has evidence revealing a man, that is an obvious danger to society.

Further information:
Appearing on charges of assault in a Pretoria court, Jaco Swart pleaded guilty to abusing his wife. He argued that the events happened in 2018 and that he is now a changed man. His wife, Nicoleen secured protection orders against him that he ignored for two years. The case of assault against him dragged on for two years and the state set him free on the first day of his trial without hearing the evidence of his wife, witnesses, former employees and a forensic expert who retrieved CCTV footage of a terrible beating. Jaco deleted the footage, but the forensic 'hacker' retrieved it. For this reason, the court argued that the footage was not authentic and that Jaco showed true remorse. The defence also told the court that Jaco has been undergoing psychological assessments and that he was deemed harmless. But these documents were never seen by the court or the complainant. The trial was set for three days. As the court was about to start, the prosecutor told everyone to exit the court and only met with Jaco and his lawyer. Although the complainant indicated that she did not want to mediate outside chambers, Jaco pleaded guilty, and the court immediately handed down a 3 year prison sentence suspended for five years and a R20 000 fine. Jaco walked out a free man, laughing in Nicoleen’s face.
Nicoleen, was not Jaco’s only victim. She says he often beat up employees who worked with the couple in their second hand car dealership that has now been shut. Nicoleen says the business was suffering because Jaco assaulted staff and clients. A man wrote on Halopeter, how Jaco beat him when he complained about a car he bought.

Jaco’s most recent attack happened the Friday before his trial when he beat up his now- estranged girlfriend in a Cape Town bar.

After the 2018 assault, Nicoleen moved to Durban to live with her folks, along with the couples' two young boys. Although she had a restraining order against Jaco, that did not stop him. He also moved to Durban, constantly harassing her and ignoring the court’s orders.
He finally moved on with his life late last year October and moved to Brackenfell in Cape Town. Here, he met Janine (wants to stay anonymous) who he dated until June 2022. She broke up with him because he was too abusive. He stalked her every day and on Friday 3 June, he attacked her in public, beating her up in the same fashion as he did, his now estranged wife, Nicoleen. When Janine’s friends, Christie and Mia, tried to assist, he broke Christie’s ribs and busted Mia’s lip.
This is the man, the court deemed remorseful.


Extra Budget Items:
flights and Accommodation in Cape Town for Presenter and producer to interview other victims and search for Jaco at his house and his business.
